claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients and healthy controls showed marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, with increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils, and eosinophils correlating with disease severity.

sources.quote: We analysed PBMC and plasma samples from patients with moderate or severe COVID-19 and healthy HCW donors by flow cytometry and ELISA to quantify leukocytes and soluble mediators, respectively.
COVID-19 patients presented with marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, even after normalization for age as a possible confounder.
In patients with COVID-19, increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils and eosinophils correlated with the severity of disease.

comparison.finding: marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in moderate COVID-19 vs healthy
marked reductions in T cell number and frequency in severe COVID-19 vs healthy
increases in monocytes, low-density neutrophils, and eosinophils in severe vs moderate COVID-19

claim_2.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed increased levels of cytokines linked to cytokine release syndrome, such as IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18, and TNF, with higher associations in severe disease.

sources.quote: We analysed PBMC and plasma samples from patients with moderate or severe COVID-19 and healthy HCW donors by flow cytometry and ELISA to quantify leukocytes and soluble mediators, respectively.
Most of the cytokines linked to cytokine release syndrome (CRS), such as IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18 and TNF, showed increased positive associations in patients with severe disease.

comparison.finding: increased levels of cytokines linked to CRS in severe vs moderate COVID-19

claim_3.claim: Real time polymerase chain reaction assay of nasopharyngeal swabs from COVID-19 patients showed no significant difference in viral RNA load between moderate and severe disease at specific time points, but a steady decline in viral load over the course of disease in moderate patients, unlike in severe patients.

sources.quote: We assessed viral RNA load (quantified by quantitative PCR with reverse transcription (RT–qPCR) using nasopharyngeal swabs).

Although there was no significant difference in viral RNA load between patients with moderate and severe disease at any specific time point analysed, patients with moderate disease showed a steady decline in viral load over the course of disease, whereas those with severe disease did not.

comparison.finding: no significant difference in viral RNA load between moderate and severe at specific time points
